items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: I think Chris Kelly was the best with that.

ctx.x: Who was good with a plunge? You're asking who was good with a plunge. Yeah. Yeah.

Well, I'd like to know who used to use the plunge of the boys. Who? Plunger. Who the best trumpet? No. Plunger. Plunger. You know that? Plunger you use with your trumpet? Oh. Let me see. Who got, who got. Oh. I see. So many of them used to do that. I think Chris Kelly was the best with that. Yeah, me too, yeah. And Feli Boo Boo too, you know. Yeah. Used to take some time of glass, a cup, you know. Yeah. Like that, you know. Sometimes used to take your hand, you know. And then that was a good jazz trombone player.…
Yeah. And Feli Boo Boo, you know. Yeah. I think it was Ducey was the jazz trombone.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: Before I left here, Bobby was playing with Chris Kelly.

ctx.x: Ask him why he's got Zeb and Ernest Kelly together. Zeb was a fine fella. You see what?

He never disappointed me. He said, why come you got Zeb and Chris Kelly together? Ernest Kelly. Ernest Kelly. Well, that's not just coming to my mind, you know. Ernest Kelly. Did they work together? He told me about Ernest Kelly, didn't he? Did they ever work together? You know, that's what I told. When we were playing together, we had to get our uniform, you know. And so I asked, I asked the man, I asked the man, why did he charge me the same thing that charged Eddie? I went, Ernest. He said, well, I said, you…
Ask him, who did Zeb work with?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: He said did you play with Chris before you played with Jack Carey? ... Oh, long before I went to Mexico. He was a good musician too. I asked Chris Kelly to tie you out before he took you in his band.

ctx.x: Well I asked him did he play with Chris before he played with Jack Carey?

He said did you play with Chris before you played with Jack Carey? Oh yeah, Jack. And I didn't forget who Chris had. Been so long. I know a long time ago before I left he used to have Faso. Yeah, no Faso is dumb or whatever.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: Chris Kelly, he was another good corner player... Do-do-do-do-dee, bo-do-do-dee... Would Chris run those chords? No, Chris played most with a plunger.

ctx.x: First was Wesley Dunn. Yeah, and second was Blue. Yeah. And third was who? What's the man this? No, ask him who the third corner.

Who was the third corner player? William Padjo. William and Ricard Ellis was the fourth. Oh, huh. And then Willie Edwards was the fifth. George McCullen was the sixth. Albert Du Conger, he was the seventh. Chris Kelly, he was another good corner player. You hear what I'm talking about? And then I played by the fellow with the third. And then Johnny Henry with the third. And then I went with Punch, you see? After Punch quit Jack Carey, where he was taking Jack's whole band. He played with him. Ask him if you…
Did you play with Jack any?
